findings.highlight: …I hope she's aware that it's hard for anybody to give a proper response to that kind of excuse before she uses it.
findings.evidenceJa:
…このネタを使われると、
人のことが言えなくなってしまうので勘弁して欲しい。
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot criticize Chiaki over family estrangement because he is in no position to talk; the English says it is hard for anybody to give a response.
findings.japanese:
…このネタを使われると、
人のことが言えなくなってしまうので勘弁して欲しい。
findings.todokanai: …I hope she's aware that it's hard for anybody to give a proper response to that kind of excuse before she uses it.

findings.highlight: It's just that as far as Izumi is concerned, I know that even if I try to complain, she'll shrug me off with a "Well, whatever" and just do whatever she wants to anyway.
findings.evidenceJa:
ただ、和泉の場合、嘘のはずの脅し文句を
『ま、いっかぁ』程度の割り切りで
実行したりしそうだからしょうがないんだ。
findings.explanation: Chiaki might turn what should be a bluff into reality with a casual shrug; the English says she ignores complaints and does whatever she wants.
findings.japanese:
ただ、和泉の場合、嘘のはずの脅し文句を
『ま、いっかぁ』程度の割り切りで
実行したりしそうだからしょうがないんだ。
findings.todokanai: It's just that as far as Izumi is concerned, I know that even if I try to complain, she'll shrug me off with a "Well, whatever" and just do whatever she wants to anyway.

findings.highlight: I neither hoped for nor approved this
findings.evidenceJa: 望まないまま、許されないまま…それでも俺の生活は、徐々に元へと戻っていく。
findings.explanation: Haruki's life is returning to normal while he still does not want that recovery and still has not been forgiven. The English assigns both verbs to Haruki—he neither hoped for nor approved it—erasing the externally unresolved fact that Setsuna has not forgiven him.
findings.japanese:
望まないまま、許されないまま…
それでも俺の生活は、徐々に元へと戻っていく。
findings.todokanai: I neither hoped for nor approved this… but my life's gradually getting back on track.

findings.highlight: Even so, my stomach, which had started to whine in the middle of it all, is now brazenly accepting chunks of cheese and dough.
findings.evidenceJa:
それでも、途中で音を上げるかと思っていた俺の胃は、
なかなか図太くチーズとパイの塊を受け入れた。
findings.explanation: Haruki expected his stomach to give up midway, but it did not; the English says it had already begun whining.
findings.japanese:
それでも、途中で音を上げるかと思っていた俺の胃は、
なかなか図太くチーズとパイの塊を受け入れた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, my stomach, which had started to whine in the middle of it all, is now brazenly accepting chunks of cheese and dough.

findings.highlight: I've made it kind of a habit
findings.evidenceJa: さすがに外泊を繰り返してたせいで先立つものが…
findings.explanation: Chiaki admits that repeatedly staying away from home has depleted the money she needs, explaining her attempt to shift more of the pizza bill onto Haruki. The English says the sleepovers have simply become a habit, deleting the financial setup and making the bargaining exchange incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「い、いや～、
さすがに外泊を繰り返してたせいで先立つものが…」
findings.todokanai: "Y-You know～ it's just that I've been sleeping over at other places for quite some time now, so I've made it kind of a habit…"

findings.highlight: "That's for the sponsor. It's the sole condition for him to provide his support."
findings.evidenceJa:
「それはスポンサーに譲れ。
資金提供の絶対条件だ」
findings.explanation: Haruki calls himself the sponsor and makes surrendering the last slice his funding condition; the English refers to the sponsor as 'him,' implying a third person.
findings.japanese:
「それはスポンサーに譲れ。
資金提供の絶対条件だ」
findings.todokanai: "That's for the sponsor. It's the sole condition for him to provide his support."

findings.highlight: I can take control of you by using that information
findings.evidenceJa: こっちは逆にそういうの全部コントロールして、相手に逆の意図を誤解させるように仕向けるの
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she controls all of those signals in herself and thereby makes the other person misread her as having the opposite intention. The English says she uses observed information to control the opponent, replacing her actorly command of her own presentation—the skill demonstrated throughout the scene—with generic mind control.
findings.japanese:
「それだけじゃないよ。
こっちは逆にそういうの全部コントロールして、
相手に逆の意図を誤解させるように仕向けるの」
findings.todokanai: "And that's not all. I can take control of you by using that information and mislead you to think and act the way I want you to."

findings.highlight: The pointless conversation goes on and on, while our eyes never leave the cards.
findings.evidenceJa:
そのギリギリの駆け引きは、
お互い、カードから目を離さないまま行われた。
findings.explanation: Their exchange is described as a razor-edge piece of maneuvering; the English calls it a pointless conversation.
findings.japanese:
そのギリギリの駆け引きは、
お互い、カードから目を離さないまま行われた。
findings.todokanai: The pointless conversation goes on and on, while our eyes never leave the cards.

findings.highlight: Do you think it will backfire on me eventually?
findings.evidenceJa: あたしはまだ、ミイラ取りのままでいられてると思う？
findings.explanation: Chiaki invokes ミイラ取りがミイラになる: the mummy hunter becomes a mummy, or the person who set out to capture someone becomes captured herself. She asks whether Haruki thinks she is still merely the hunter—whether she has avoided falling for her own subject. The English reduces this present identity question to a vague possibility that something may backfire eventually.
findings.japanese:
「ね、春希…
あたしはまだ、ミイラ取りのままでいられてると思う？」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, Haruki… Do you think it will backfire on me eventually?"

findings.highlight: I'm able to properly let my feelings out
findings.evidenceJa: けれど、ちゃんと相手には伝わったから。
findings.explanation: Haruki consoles himself that, despite failing to say the crucial words himself, the intended meaning properly reached the other person. The English says only that he was able to let his feelings out, replacing successful reception by Chiaki with successful self-expression.
findings.japanese: けれど、ちゃんと相手には伝わったから。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I'm able to properly let my feelings out.

findings.highlight: "That's impossible… I have confidence in that myself."
findings.evidenceJa:
「あるわけないだろそんなこと…
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はある」
findings.explanation: Haruki echoes Chiaki's earlier formulation that he is confident he has been involved with her enough to know she is no wicked woman; the English reduces this to confidence in himself.
findings.japanese:
「あるわけないだろそんなこと…
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はある」
findings.todokanai: "That's impossible… I have confidence in that myself."

findings.evidenceJa: 物語にしても遜色のない、あんたたちの綺麗な想いを知ってるよ？
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she knows the beautiful feelings belonging to all of 'you'—あんたたち, the people in Haruki's story—feelings worthy of a story. The English reduces this explicitly plural emotional structure to one beautiful feeling belonging to Haruki alone.
findings.japanese:
「物語にしても遜色のない、
あんたたちの綺麗な想いを知ってるよ？」
findings.todokanai: "That beautiful feeling of yours that's on par with any of the world's many stories, you know what I mean?"
